title: Media ja uutiset
subtitle: Media & news
focus_note:
Participles work like adjectives and often replace a relative clause. The VA participle (-va/-vä) is present active: lehteä lukeva mies = mies, joka lukee lehteä. The NUT participle (-nut/-nyt, plural -neet) is past active: uutiset katsoneet ihmiset = ihmiset, jotka katsoivat uutiset. The agent participle (-ma/-mä) needs a genitive doer: toimittajan kirjoittama artikkeli = artikkeli, jonka toimittaja kirjoitti.
The passive past participle (-ttu/-tu) means 'done': eniten luettu artikkeli. All participles inflect like adjectives: kirjoittaman, tapahtuneesta.

vocab.example_translation: In the morning I read a news story online about a traffic accident.

vocab.example: Olemme tilanneet paikallista sanomalehteä jo monta vuotta.
vocab.example_translation: We have subscribed to the local newspaper for many years.

vocab.example: Toimittaja haastatteli ministeriä eilen illan uutisiin.
vocab.example_translation: The journalist interviewed the minister yesterday for the evening news.
The radio interviewed a well-known climate researcher in the morning.
I wrote an article about climate change for the school paper.
Unfortunately the headline of the news story was misleading.

vocab.example: Lehti julkaisi tutkimuksen tulokset tänä aamuna.
vocab.example_translation: The paper published the results of the study this morning.
The live broadcast starts at eight o'clock.
Many people read news on social media.

vocab.example: Valeuutiset leviävät nopeasti verkossa ja sosiaalisessa mediassa.
vocab.example_translation: Fake news spreads quickly online and on social media.
The information spread quickly throughout the town.

vocab.example: Tarkista aina uutisen lähde ennen kuin jaat sen.
vocab.example_translation: Always check the source of the news before you share it.
Tell us your own opinion on the matter at the meeting.
Many people commented on the news online.

vocab.example: Sananvapaus on yksi demokratian tärkeimmistä periaatteista.
vocab.example_translation: Freedom of speech is one of the most important principles of democracy.
The police announced the accident late in the evening.
The company sent a press release to the media in the morning.
I subscribed to the digital version of the magazine for a whole year.
A lot of ads were shown during the programme.

vocab.example: Ohjelmalla oli ensimmäisenä iltana miljoona katsojaa.
vocab.example_translation: The programme had a million viewers on the first evening.

vocab.example: Ohjelma käsittelee ajankohtaisia aiheita joka torstai.
vocab.example_translation: The programme deals with current topics every Thursday.
It's worth being critical when reading the news.
The media greatly influences people's opinions.

vocab.example: Tapahtumasta kerrottiin seuraavana päivänä kaikissa lehdissä.
vocab.example_translation: The event was reported in all the papers the next day.

drills.translation: The train leaving for Helsinki is late.
I read the news about the accident that happened yesterday.
This is a press release written by the minister.
The people watching the programme are excited.
I read the article written by the journalist.
The news published yesterday interested everyone.
All readers who have subscribed to the paper get a gift.
The man arrested by the police has been released.
The rapidly growing problem worries experts.
The journalist who interviewed the president won a prize.
This is the paper's most-read article.
The programme starting tomorrow deals with the climate.

drills.prompt: Muuta relatiivilause VA-partisiipiksi: Mies, joka lukee lehteä, on isäni.
drills.note: joka lukee → lukeva; the object stays before the participle
drills.translation: The man reading the paper is my father.

drills.prompt: Muuta relatiivilause agenttipartisiipiksi: Artikkeli, jonka toimittaja kirjoitti, oli kiinnostava.
drills.translation: The article written by the journalist was interesting.

drills.prompt: Muuta relatiivilause NUT-partisiipiksi: Ihmiset, jotka katsoivat uutiset, olivat järkyttyneitä.
drills.translation: The people who watched the news were shocked.
